## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates practical supply chain security controls in multi-cloud Kubernetes environments. It assesses familiarity with policy-as-code, container image signature verification, and SBOM (Software Bill of Materials) attestations integrated into CI/CD pipelines.

- **Image Provenance:** Cosign and Sigstore provide cryptographic verification that container images have not been tampered with and originate from trusted sources.

- **Policy-as-Code:** Gatekeeper and Kyverno enforce admission control policies as code, ensuring consistent security enforcement across clusters.
- **Multi-Cloud Complexity:** Different cloud providers require unified security controls; policy engines provide a vendor-agnostic approach to image verification.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This tests practical security tooling integration and explains how to enforce image signing early.

## Key Concepts
- Image signing with cosign
- Manifest parsing to collect images
- CI integration (GitHub Actions) and local validation

## Code Example
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
PUBKEY=${COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY:-cosign.pub}
for f in manifests/**/*.yaml; do
  images=$(yq e '.. | .image? // empty' "$f" 2>/dev/null)
  for img in $images; do
    cosign verify --key "$PUBKEY" "$img" || { echo "Unsigned: $img"; exit 1; }
  done
done
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle dynamic image tags vs. digests in this gate?
- How would you test the workflow locally before opening a PR?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of namespace isolation and basic egress filtering using NetworkPolicy. It checks hands-on ability to craft minimal, enforceable rules and verify them.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes NetworkPolicy basics
- Namespace-scoped isolation
- Egress rules and default deny
- Basic verification via kubectl and logs

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: test-egress-isolate
  namespace: test
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.1.2.3/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector: {}
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: dns
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 0.0.0.0/0
        except:
        - 255.255.255.255/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 53
```

```yaml
# Compliant Pod in test namespace
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-pod
  namespace: test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 300"]
```

```yaml
# Noncompliant Pod in test namespace (tries to access prod)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-pod
  namespace: test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "wget http://prod.svc.cluster.local || true"]
```

```yaml
# DNS test Pod (for compliance with DNS allow rule)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: dns-test
  namespace: test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "nslookup kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local"]
```

## Follow-up Steps
- kubectl apply -f policy.yaml
- kubectl apply -f compliant-pod.yaml; kubectl exec compliant-pod -- curl logs.internal:443
- kubectl apply -f noncompliant-pod.yaml; observe failure to reach prod
- Check events: kubectl describe networkpolicy/test-egress-isolate -n test

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to encode security baselines as policy-as-code and enforce them in CI/CD pipelines for multi-tenant clusters. It tests understanding of threat modeling, policy granularity, and how to allow exceptions in a controlled manner.

## Key Concepts

- **Open Policy Agent (OPA) with Rego**: Declarative policy language for Kubernetes admission control
- **Pod Security Standards**: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, privilege escalation, and security profiles
- **Volume Security**: hostPath, hostNetwork, and hostPID considerations in multi-tenant environments

## Rego Policy

```rego
package kubernetes.admission

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  container := input.request.object.spec.containers[_]
  container.securityContext.runAsNonRoot != true
  msg := "Containers must run as non-root (runAsNonRoot: true)"
}

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  container := input.request.object.spec.containers[_]
  container.securityContext.privileged == true
  msg := "Privileged containers are not allowed"
}

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  container := input.request.object.spec.containers[_]
  container.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem != true
  msg := "Containers must use readOnlyRootFilesystem"
}

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  input.request.object.spec.hostNetwork == true
  msg := "hostNetwork is not allowed"
}

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  input.request.object.spec.hostPID == true
  msg := "hostPID is not allowed"
}

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  volume := input.request.object.spec.volumes[_]
  volume.hostPath
  not allowed_hostpath[volume.hostPath.path]
  msg := sprintf("hostPath volume %s is not allowed", [volume.hostPath.path])
}

allowed_hostpath {
  input.request.namespace == "kube-system"
}

allowed_hostpath[path] {
  allowed_paths := [""]
  path := allowed_paths[_]
}
```

## Failing Manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: insecure-pod
  namespace: default
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: false
      privileged: true
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: false
  hostNetwork: true
  hostPID: true
  volumes:
  - name: data
    hostPath:
      path: /var/data
```

## Passing Manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secure-pod
  namespace: production
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:stable
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: true
      privileged: false
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      seccompProfile:
        type: RuntimeDefault
  securityContext:
    seccompProfile:
      type: RuntimeDefault
  volumes:
  - name: cache
    emptyDir: {}
```

## CI Verification Steps

1. **Install OPA CLI**: `brew install opa` or download from https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/
2. **Test Rego policy**: `opa eval --format pretty --data policy.rego --input failing-pod.json "data.kubernetes.admission.deny"`
3. **Verify failing manifest**: Should return denial messages for each violated policy
4. **Verify passing manifest**: Should return empty deny array
5. **CI/CD Integration**: Add OPA gate to your pipeline:
   ```yaml
   # GitHub Actions example
   - name: Run OPA Gate
     run: |
       opa eval --format json --data policy.rego --input pod.json "data.kubernetes.admission.deny" > results.json
       if [ $(jq '.result[0].expressions[0].value | length' results.json) -gt 0 ]; then
         echo "Policy violations found:"
         jq '.result[0].expressions[0].value' results.json
         exit 1
       fi
   ```
6. **Deploy to cluster**: Apply the OPA Gatekeeper constraints via Gatekeeper's ConstraintTemplate system.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design runtime security controls that span CI, policy engines, and multi cloud networking, ensuring outbound traffic is strictly controlled and auditable.

## Key Concepts

- Policy-as-code (Gatekeeper/OPA)
- Egress gateway design and TLS origination
- Outbound allowlist management
- CI validation for policy enforcement
- Cross-cloud consistency and testing

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate for Gatekeeper enforcing egress gateway annotation
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8segressgateway
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sEgressPolicy
  targets:
  - target: obj  # pseudo example for clarity
    rego: |
      package k8segress
      default deny = true
      deny[msg] = msg {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        not input.review.object.metadata.annotations["egress.gateway/enforced"] == "true"
        msg := "Pod must set egress.gateway/enforced=true to route via central gateway"
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint demonstrating allowlist usage (illustrative)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sEgressPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-egress-gateway
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        kinds: ["Pod"]
  parameters:
    allowlist: ["app.allowed.example.com"]
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (no egress annotation or disallowed destination)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: bad-egress-pod
  annotations:
    # missing or false
    egress.gateway/enforced: "false"
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (annotation set and allowlisted destination)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: good-egress-pod
  annotations:
    egress.gateway/enforced: "true"
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:1.23.4
```

## Local and CI Validation

- Local: run gatekeeper locally to test ConstraintTemplate/Constraint; simulate Pod admission with k8s manifest.

## Why This Is Asked

In production Kubernetes environments, ensuring supply-chain security for Helm-based deployments is critical. This question evaluates your ability to integrate multiple security tools—Helm templating, SBOM generation, and image signature verification—into a cohesive CI gate. It tests practical knowledge of enforcing provenance and attestations before code merges.

## Key Concepts

- **Helm templating and values extraction**: Rendering charts to discover all container images referenced in deployments
- **SBOM generation**: Using Syft to create a CycloneDX SBOM that catalogs all dependencies and artifacts
- **Image signing verification**: Using cosign to validate container image signatures against a public key stored in the repository
- **CI gate integration**: Implementing fail-fast behavior in GitHub Actions to block unsigned images and missing attestations

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow for Helm image signing enforcement
name: Helm Image Security Gate

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  helm-security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3

      - name: Install Helm and Syft
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/syft/main/install.sh | sh

      - name: Render Helm templates
        run: helm template my-app ./chart --values values.yaml --output-dir ./rendered

      - name: Extract image references
        run: |
          grep -rh 'image:' ./rendered | awk '{print $2}' > images.txt

      - name: Generate SBOM with Syft
        run: |
          syft $(cat images.txt) -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json

      - name: Verify image signatures with cosign
        run: |
          COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY=cosign.pub
          for IMAGE in $(cat images.txt); do
            cosign verify --key $COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY $IMAGE || exit 1
          done
```
